runs.v: is a single-ply synthetic-rubber membrane installed on flat and low-slope commercial roofs to seal the building against water entry. EPDM roofing systems attach mechanically, fully adhere, or hold under ballast, with the splice seams joining the sheets.

The membrane is an elastomeric compound of ethylene, propylene, and a diene monomer, and like other single-ply membranes it is a staple of low-slope roofing on residential and commercial roofs. EPDM features strong resistance to UV radiation, ozone, and extreme temperature cycling and has a low embodied energy in production. It comes in black, which owes its UV resistance to carbon black and absorbs heat, or in white to reflect it, and its smooth surface sheds water. Membranes typically come in 45-, 60-, and 90-mil thicknesses, and thicker membranes offer greater puncture resistance and extended longevity; wide sheets cover commercial flat roofs with few seams, while narrower widths suit mechanically fastened applications, where the fastener rows run in the laps.

faqs.q: How long does a commercial EPDM roof last in West Orange?

runs.v: A commercial EPDM rubber membrane lasts 15 to 25 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, with some service-life studies placing EPDM at 25 to 30 years. EPDM outlasts TPO at 7 to 20 years and modified bitumen at 20 years on the same chart, with seam separation the failure mode that ends EPDM service.

faqs.q: Why choose EPDM over TPO for a West Orange commercial flat roof?

runs.v: EPDM rubber membrane records 15 to 25 years and TPO 7 to 20 years, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart. EPDM fails most often at the splice seams and TPO at the welded seams, per NRCA technical guidance, so a Newark Quality Roofing assessment matches the membrane to the building and its ridge-side exposure off the First Watchung slopes.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a commercial EPDM roof in West Orange?

runs.v: Yes for a full installation: EPDM installation on a commercial building requires a construction permit, because New Jersey's Uniform Construction Code limits the ordinary-maintenance exemption to repair of up to 25% of the total roof area in a 12-month period, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, and the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode requires complete removal of a water-soaked covering or a roof already carrying two or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4. Confirm with the West Orange construction office before work.

faqs.q: When should a commercial EPDM roof be replaced instead of repaired?

runs.v: Replace a commercial EPDM roof when membrane damage exceeds 25 to 30% of the roof area, when leaks recur at the same location, or when the membrane reaches 15 to 25 years of service. The 25 to 30% flat-roof threshold traces to Modernize and HomeGuide flat-roof guidance, and a recurring same-spot leak signals systemic failure regardless of damaged area, per HomeAdvisor.

faqs.q: Can you install EPDM over an existing ballasted roof in West Orange?

runs.v: Removing the ballast and the existing membrane is the durable path rather than overlaying, because the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode requires complete removal of a water-soaked covering or a roof already carrying two or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4. A Newark Quality Roofing scope strips the ballast and old membrane, repairs the deck, and installs a new fully adhered or mechanically attached EPDM system graded to drain.
